podcast.title: Fanbase
podcast.body: The Vandals enjoyed a notable fanbase among prominent figures in alternative rock, including Kurt Cobain and Eddie Vedder, indicating their influence and appeal within the wider rock community. "Kurt Cobain was a fan of the vandals, and so is Eddie Vetter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Humorous West Coast Punk
podcast.body: Formed in Huntington Beach in 1980, The Vandals were known for injecting humor and a "goofy" attitude into the West Coast punk scene. They loved punk but consciously chose not to take themselves too seriously, setting them apart. "Some of the other proto pop punks thought it was time to lighten up and inject some humor into the whole West Coast punk scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tony Hawk Video Game Feature
podcast.body: Music from The Vandals was featured in Tony Hawk's popular skateboarding video games. "Tony Hawk's video games sold by the millions, and each one featured appropriate music from groups like The Vandals and Laguewagon, Suicidal tendencies, Millen-Call and Bad Religion, and so many more."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: California Hardcore Scene
xref.body: The Offspring were deeply rooted in the California hardcore scene, a fierce but small community dedicated to punk that evolved from the original 1970s punk. This music became a soundtrack for skaters and snowboarders, including bands like Dead Kennedys, The Adolescents, The Vandals, Black Flag, and Bad Religion, which was niche and rarely played on radio. "Everyone was into California hardcore. The punk that evolved out of the original punk of the 1970s. The scene was small but fierce and its adherents stuck together. And some of this music became the soundtrack for skaters and snowboarders, dead candidates, the adolescence, the vandals, black flag, bad religion, really niche stuff at the time, and certainly stuff that never made it on the radio."
